resource.name: aws_secretsmanager_secret
resource.description: Provides a resource to manage AWS Secrets Manager secret metadata. To manage secret rotation, see the aws_secretsmanager_secret_rotation resource. To manage a secret value, see the aws_secretsmanager_secret_version resource.
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_secretsmanager_secret` Terraform resource enables the creation and management of metadata for secrets stored in AWS Secrets Manager, supporting secure storage and access to sensitive information such as API keys, credentials, and configuration data. Common use cases include setting up centralized secret management for applications, automating secret lifecycle processes, and integrating secrets with AWS services or external systems. Users can configure attributes like name, description, tags, and policies to control access, while pairing this resource with `aws_secretsmanager_secret_version` for managing secret values and `aws_secretsmanager_secret_rotation` for automated rotation workflows.

examples.title: Basic
examples.llm_summary: "Demonstrates the basic configuration of the `aws_secretsmanager_secret` resource by creating a Secrets Manager secret with a specified name. This example is ideal for users looking to understand the minimal setup required to define a secret in AWS Secrets Manager using Terraform."

arguments.name: description
arguments.llm_summary: The `description` argument for the `aws_secretsmanager_secret` resource allows users to define a human-readable explanation or context for the secret, helping to document its purpose or usage within the Secrets Manager. Setting this argument enhances clarity and organization, especially in environments with multiple secrets, by providing metadata that aids in identification and management.

arguments.name: force_overwrite_replica_secret
arguments.description: (Optional) Accepts boolean value to specify whether to overwrite a secret with the same name in the destination Region.
arguments.llm_summary: The `force_overwrite_replica_secret` argument in the `aws_secretsmanager_secret` resource allows users to control whether a secret with the same name in a destination region is automatically overwritten during replication. Setting this to `true` ensures seamless updates to replicated secrets, supporting use cases like cross-region secret synchronization or disaster recovery configurations.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument for the `aws_secretsmanager_secret` resource represents the unique identifier of the secret, typically auto-generated by AWS upon creation. While optional, specifying this argument allows users to reference or manage an existing secret by its ID, enabling workflows such as importing or updating pre-existing secrets within Terraform configurations.

arguments.name: kms_key_id
arguments.description: (Optional) ARN or Id of the AWS KMS key to be used to encrypt the secret values in the versions stored in this secret. If you need to reference a CMK in a different account, you can use only the key ARN. If you don't specify this value, then Secrets Manager defaults to using the AWS account's default KMS key (the one named `aws/secretsmanager`). If the default KMS key with that name doesn't yet exist, then AWS Secrets Manager creates it for you automatically the first time.
arguments.llm_summary: The `kms_key_id` argument in the `aws_secretsmanager_secret` resource allows users to specify the AWS KMS key (by ARN or ID) used to encrypt secret values stored in the secret's versions. By defining this argument, users can control encryption behavior, enabling the use of a custom KMS key for enhanced security or cross-account key management, or defaulting to the account's automatically provisioned KMS key (`aws/secretsmanager`) if unspecified.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: (Optional) Friendly name of the new secret. The secret name can consist of uppercase letters, lowercase letters, digits, and any of the following characters: `/_+=.@-` Conflicts with `name_prefix`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `name` argument for the `aws_secretsmanager_secret` resource allows users to define a unique, human-readable identifier for the secret, enabling easier organization and retrieval within AWS Secrets Manager. By specifying this argument, users can assign a custom name to the secret, which is useful for aligning secrets with application environments, roles, or specific use cases. Note that it conflicts with `name_prefix`, offering flexibility in naming conventions.

arguments.name: name_prefix
arguments.description: (Optional) Creates a unique name beginning with the specified prefix. Conflicts with `name`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `name_prefix` argument for the `aws_secretsmanager_secret` resource allows users to define a custom prefix for the secret's name, enabling the creation of a unique, system-generated name that begins with the specified prefix. This is useful for managing naming conventions, avoiding name conflicts, and dynamically generating secret names, particularly in environments where multiple secrets are created programmatically.

arguments.name: policy
arguments.description: (Optional) Valid JSON document representing a resource policy. For more information about building AWS IAM policy documents with Terraform, see the AWS IAM Policy Document Guide. Removing `policy` from your configuration or setting `policy` to null or an empty string (i.e., `policy = ""`) will not delete the policy since it could have been set by `aws_secretsmanager_secret_policy`. To delete the `policy`, set it to `"{}"` (an empty JSON document).
arguments.llm_summary: The `policy` argument for the `aws_secretsmanager_secret` resource allows users to define a resource-based IAM policy in JSON format, specifying access control rules for the secret. By configuring this argument, users can manage permissions for who can access or modify the secret, aligning with security and compliance goals for sensitive data management.

arguments.name: recovery_window_in_days
arguments.description: (Optional) Number of days that AWS Secrets Manager waits before it can delete the secret. This value can be `0` to force deletion without recovery or range from `7` to `30` days. The default value is `30`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `recovery_window_in_days` argument for the `aws_secretsmanager_secret` resource allows users to define the lifecycle behavior of a secret by specifying the number of days AWS Secrets Manager will retain the secret in a recoverable state before permanent deletion. This configuration supports user goals related to secret management and recovery, enabling control over retention periods for accidental deletions or compliance requirements, with options ranging from immediate deletion (`0`) to a recovery window of up to 30 days.

arguments.name: tags
arguments.description: (Optional) Key-value map of user-defined tags that are attached to the secret. If configured with a provider `default_tags` configuration block present, tags with matching keys will overwrite those defined at the provider-level.
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags` argument for the `aws_secretsmanager_secret` resource allows users to define a key-value map of custom metadata to categorize and organize secrets, such as associating them with environments, projects, or cost centers. By setting this argument, users can enhance resource discoverability, streamline management, and integrate tagging strategies for governance or billing purposes, with provider-level `default_tags` being overridden for matching keys.

arguments.name: tags_all
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags_all` argument for the `aws_secretsmanager_secret` resource allows users to define a comprehensive set of key-value tags that are applied to the secret, including inherited tags from the provider's default configuration. This enables streamlined resource organization, cost allocation, and metadata management across AWS services, supporting common goals like tagging for environments, ownership, or compliance tracking.

blocks.name: replica
blocks.description: (Optional) Configuration block to support secret replication. See details below.

arguments.name: kms_key_id
arguments.description: (Optional) ARN, Key ID, or Alias of the AWS KMS key within the region secret is replicated to. If one is not specified, then Secrets Manager defaults to using the AWS account's default KMS key (`aws/secretsmanager`) in the region or creates one for use if non-existent.
arguments.llm_summary: The `kms_key_id` argument for the `replica` configuration in the `aws_secretsmanager_secret` resource allows users to specify the AWS KMS key (via ARN, Key ID, or Alias) used to encrypt the replicated secret in the target region. By setting this argument, users can control the encryption behavior and ensure the replica uses a specific KMS key for compliance, security, or organizational requirements; otherwise, the default KMS key (`aws/secretsmanager`) is used.

arguments.name: last_accessed_date
arguments.llm_summary: The `last_accessed_date` argument for the `replica` in the `aws_secretsmanager_secret` resource allows users to specify or track the timestamp when the replica secret was last accessed. While not required, this argument can be used to monitor access patterns or audit usage, supporting goals like compliance, security analysis, or optimizing secret management workflows.

arguments.name: region
arguments.llm_summary: The `region` argument for the `replica` configuration in the `aws_secretsmanager_secret` resource specifies the AWS region where the secret will be replicated, enabling cross-region availability and redundancy. By defining this required parameter, users can ensure secure access to the secret in the specified region, supporting disaster recovery, compliance, and multi-region application architectures.

arguments.name: status
arguments.llm_summary: The `status` argument for the `replica` block in the `aws_secretsmanager_secret` resource allows users to specify the replication status of a secret in a target region, such as enabling or disabling replication. This configuration helps manage the availability and synchronization of secrets across multiple regions, supporting disaster recovery and multi-region architectures.

arguments.name: status_message
arguments.llm_summary: The `status_message` argument for the `replica` block in the `aws_secretsmanager_secret` resource allows users to retrieve a descriptive message about the current status of the replica secret. This provides insight into operational details or issues related to the replication process, aiding in monitoring and troubleshooting replication behavior.

blocks.llm_summary: The `replica` configuration block in the `aws_secretsmanager_secret` resource enables secret replication across multiple AWS regions, ensuring high availability and disaster recovery. It encapsulates settings related to defining target regions for replication, allowing users to securely distribute secrets to meet compliance, redundancy, or multi-region application requirements.
